archetype.name: Retooling (defense ahead of offense)
archetype.definition: A recent contender coming off a collapse whose defense has recovered to league-average while the offense stalls without its injured point guard.

report.headline: Real defensive repair, a broken offense, and everything hinging on Haliburton's return
report.take:
Indiana is 3-7, but this is not last season's 19-63 team in a new month. The defense has climbed from 24th to 15th in Def Rank, and its DRtg of 113.6 sits right at the league average after last year's 118.8. The interior is the cause. Opponents are shooting 60.9% at the rim, fifth-best in the league and well under the league's 65.2%, after 66.0% a year ago. That is the most important sign of health on the sheet.

The offense is the problem, and it has a name attached. Tyrese Haliburton played four games and looked like the player the Pacers' recent playoff runs were built around: 4th of 83 on the point guard tab, a +7.6 BPM, +12.4 On-Off, 63.4 TS %. He is listed as out. Without him the ORtg is 109.7, 22nd in the league. The 3-point shooting is 25th at 32.6% on a slightly above-average share of threes, and the team is last in ORB % at 21.0. A team that misses a lot of threes and gets none of them back has no second source of offense.

The record itself is roughly honest. W vs Pt Diff is -1, so the margin implies four wins rather than three, and the Net Rtg of -3.9 ranks 19th. That describes a below-average team, not a hopeless one. The trend is what worries: scoring fell from 116.67 a game in October to 100.75 in November, and the last five games came in at 105.6 a game with a 1-4 record. The sheet doesn't say which four games Haliburton played. The way the offense has hollowed out lately fits his absence, but that is an inference.

The wing rotation is a drag on its own terms. Aaron Nesmith (-11.8 On-Off) and Kelly Oubre Jr. (-16.9) take big minutes with sub-par efficiency, and the group grades D-. Bench pieces Quenton Jackson (+12.8) and Jalen Slawson (+17.5) are posting the lineups' best numbers. Expect drift toward the mid-20s in wins on the current pace until Haliburton returns. If he does, this defense gives him a far better floor than last year's team had.

strengths.title: Rim protection has rebuilt the defense
strengths.body: Opponents are finishing at 60.9% near the rim, fifth in the league, after 66.0% last season. That interior resistance is why the DRtg has moved from 118.8 to a league-average 113.6. Rim numbers this early can swing, but it is a structural change rather than opponents simply missing threes: Opp 3P % is actually worse than the league's.

strengths.title: Haliburton is still elite
strengths.body: In four games Haliburton ranked 4th among point guards with a +7.6 BPM and a +12.4 On-Off. He is the reason the backcourt grades B while the other groups sink. The small sample cuts both ways, but nothing in it suggests decline. Availability is the only question.

concerns.title: No shooting, no second chances
concerns.body: The Pacers hit 32.6% from three, 25th in the league, and are last in ORB % at 21.0. That combination caps the offense at a 109.7 ORtg. The poor shooting may lift somewhat with Haliburton creating looks. The offensive rebounding has sat near the bottom for years and is a style choice, so it won't change.

concerns.title: Wings and frontcourt rotation sinking lineups
concerns.body: Nesmith and Oubre carry the wing minutes with BPMs of -5.4 and -4.6 and the worst On-Off marks on the roster. The group grades D-. The frontcourt grades F despite Siakam and Toppin: Jarace Walker's 47.1 TS % in heavy minutes drags it down. This is a rotation problem the coaching staff can partly address by shifting minutes toward Slawson and Toppin.

concerns.title: Offense collapsing lately
concerns.body: The last five games produced 105.6 points a game, 4.7 below the season average, with a 1-4 record. November's 100.75 a game is far off October's 116.67. Until the shooting or the point guard situation changes, this is the team's current level, not a dip.

trend.note: A 2-4 October with a functioning offense gave way to a 1-3 start to November in which scoring dropped off sharply. The defense has held roughly steady, so the slide is all on offense.

weekAhead.headline: Three winning teams around one winnable home game against Washington
weekAhead.body:
Four games: at Dallas, home for Washington and New York, then at Philadelphia. Indiana already lost to Dallas (105-121) and Philadelphia (109-114) at home this season. Three of the four opponents sit in the top 10 in defensive rank, which is the worst possible matchup for an offense ranked 22nd. Dallas leads the league in Opp 3P % at 30.6, and Philadelphia is second at 31.6.

Washington is the clear opportunity. Its -4.8 Net Rtg is a shade worse than Indiana's, and it is a bottom-four rebounding team. New York is the opposite problem: first in REB % and second in ORB %, against a Pacers team that is last on the offensive glass. Philadelphia's 9-2 comes with a league-high +2 W vs Pt Diff, so it is beatable, but on the road. One win is the baseline and two would be a good week.

keyMatchups.title: Washington is the must-win
keyMatchups.body: The Wizards rank 21st in Net Rtg and 23rd in Off Rank, essentially Indiana's peer. They allow small forwards well above their usual production (+3.45 points over their averages, 28th) and give centers extra rebounds. That is a rare chance for the struggling Indiana wings and bigs to find production.

keyMatchups.title: The Knicks' glass against Indiana's
keyMatchups.body: New York is first in REB % and DRB % and second in ORB %. Indiana is 30th in ORB % and 28th in REB %. Expect the Pacers to get almost no second chances and to give up plenty, which magnifies every missed three.

keyMatchups.title: Nembhard's lanes at shooting guard
keyMatchups.body: Dallas lets shooting guards score 4.77 points over their own averages, 28th in the league, and Washington allows 32 a game to the position. With Haliburton out, Andrew Nembhard is the guard most likely to cash in on those weaknesses.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Haliburton returns: every other number this week depends on who runs the offense.

restOfSeason.body:
On the current pace this is a 25-win team, and the Net Rtg of -3.9 says that is about right for the roster as it has played. The defense looks real: the rim protection and a league-average DRtg are a clear break from last season. The offense is running below where shooting and creation should settle with a healthy point guard. With Haliburton back for a large share of the season, a final total of 27 to 36 wins is plausible, which keeps the Pacers near the play-in line in a soft Central. Without him, the bottom of that range or below is likelier.

The close-game luck is neutral, so there is no hidden regression either way in the record. The 3-point percentage is the stat most likely to move up. The offensive rebounding is not.
swingFactors: Wing minutes shifting away from the -15 On-Off group

confidence.note: Ten games played, and the star's status and return date are unknown.
